name: Graph Theory
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of networks, connectivity, and combinatorial structures. Maps graph-theoretic concepts—vertices, edges, adjacency, paths, cycles, trees, connectivity, and graph invariants—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving networks, relationships, flows, social structures, and the mathematics of pairwise connections.

x.note: The depth anchor—a fundamental invariant that characterizes the graph (e.g., chromatic number, genus). The invariant that distinguishes graph types.

y.note: The relational anchor—the measure of how well the graph is connected (e.g., vertex connectivity, edge connectivity, second eigenvalue of Laplacian).

z.note: The transformational anchor—whether the graph can be drawn without edge crossings (planar) and how it is embedded in a surface.

0.note: The point of observation—a distinguished vertex (e.g., root of a tree, source in flow network). The reference for distances and orientations.

1.note: The boundary—the whole graph structure defined by its vertex set and edge set. The container of all connectivity.

2.note: Primitive—a fundamental unit of the graph. The building blocks of the network.

3.note: The invariant law—the relationship that edges connect vertices. The rule that defines adjacency and incidence.

4.note: The fundamental relation—a connection between two vertices (directed or undirected). The grammar of adjacency.

5.note: The pattern—a template or recurring substructure (e.g., clique, cycle, tree). The blueprint of local connectivity.

6.note: The transformation—an operation that modifies the graph (e.g., vertex deletion, edge contraction, subdivision). The process of graph evolution.

7.note: The realization—a concrete graph instance with specific vertices and edges. The actualized network.

8.note: The granularity—the number of vertices (n) and edges (m). n controls the scale of the graph.

9.note: The event—a sequence of edges connecting vertices. The moment of traversal or connectivity.

a.note: Pure potential—the maximum connectivity where every pair of vertices is adjacent. The ocean of all possible connections.

b.note: The arena—the space of all graphs with given parameters. The chaotic realm where edges appear with probability p.

c.note: Directional bias—whether edges are directed (asymmetric) or undirected (symmetric). The gradient that imposes flow.

d.note: Persistent structure—a minimal connected subgraph that spans all vertices. The memory of connectivity without cycles.

e.note: The active algorithm—a procedure that processes the graph (e.g., BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Max-Flow). The process that extracts structure.

f.note: The resonant cavity—a property or class of graphs that is closed under certain operations (e.g., forests, planar graphs). The limit of graph constructions.

values.n=3: Three vertices — triangle, path of length 2

phase.special: For bipartite graphs, phase = π (two colors); for complete graphs, phases equally spaced.
phase.significance: Phase encodes the assignment of colors or the cyclic order in a graph embedding.

adjacency.description: The Factor viewed as an adjacency matrix or incidence structure
adjacency.phase_condition: Phase as adjacency weight—0 for no edge, π for edge

geometric.description: The Factor viewed as a graph embedded in a surface (planar, toroidal)
geometric.phase_condition: Phase as embedding coordinates or face angles

spectral.description: The Factor viewed through eigenvalues of adjacency or Laplacian matrix
spectral.phase_condition: Phase as eigenvalue argument (for complex eigenvalues in directed graphs)

combinatorial.description: The Factor viewed as a combinatorial structure (cliques, colorings, matchings)
combinatorial.phase_condition: Phase as indicator of property existence (0 for absent, π for present)

creating_anew.note: When creating a graph, start with vertices (node 2) and decide on edges (node 4). Consider properties like connectivity (node y) and planarity (node z). Use algorithms (node e) to explore structure.

translating_known.complete_graph_K_n: Map to node a as complete graph, node n as order, node 4 as all possible edges
translating_known.tree_T: Map to node d as spanning tree, node 9 as unique path between vertices, node y as vertex connectivity 1
translating_known.bipartite_graph: Map to node b as bipartite, node φ as π (two colors), node y as odd cycle absence
translating_known.planar_graph: Map to node z as planar, node f as Euler's formula closure, node 8 as face count

temporary_note.special: Vertex set defined but edges not yet specified. Awaiting the pattern of connections.

constraints.simple_graph: Unless specified otherwise, graphs are simple (no loops, no multiple edges). Multigraphs require type_context.
constraints.handshaking_lemma: Sum of degrees = 2|E|, invariant that must hold.
constraints.euler_characteristic: For planar graphs, V - E + F = 2 (for connected, planar).
constraints.stratum_preference: global for general graph theory; trefoil_g for graph operations; trefoil_c for graph classes; fig8 for random graphs and hypergraphs.
